description: Cut one or more clips from YouTube videos (including streams that are live right now) in parallel. Only the requested sections are downloaded. Jobs can span different videos. Returns a result per job; failures don't abort the batch. Live results include the wall-clock range covered. Viral clips take ~15-60s each; if the batch isn't done within waitSec, you get finished results plus a jobId: call get_clips with it until pending is 0.

accent.description: Viral: highlight colour for the spoken word, default "#FFE600"

background.description: Viral: background colour behind the video, default "#000000". The full frame is always shown, never cropped.

end.description: Seconds (83) or "1:23" / "1:02:03.5". Negative = from the end ("-0:30"). For LIVE streams: "now", negative offsets from the live edge (-90), or ISO time ("2026-10-08T00:40:00Z"); roughly the last hour is available.

label.description: Short name used for the output file

precise.description: Live only: frame-accurate cut (slower re-encode). Default snaps start to a keyframe ≤5s earlier.

start.description: Seconds (83) or "1:23" / "1:02:03.5". Negative = from the end ("-0:30"). For LIVE streams: "now", negative offsets from the live edge (-90), or ISO time ("2026-10-08T00:40:00Z"); roughly the last hour is available.

style.description: "viral" = ready-to-post 1080x1920 short: hook header + the full video frame (never cropped, laid out to suit its shape) + word-by-word captions

title.description: Viral: the header hook (write a punchy one, ≤ ~10 words). Defaults to the video title

vertical.description: Plain 9:16 version: whole frame on black, no header/captions

waitSec.description: Seconds to wait before returning, default 40. If clips are still rendering, the response includes a jobId; collect the rest with get_clips.

name: create_clips
